content.what_it_is: MATLAB overlay plotter for nested Grid A and Grid B elevation snapshots: it loads snapshot 0100 from two fixed directories, constructs grid-specific x coordinates (lines 2-17), creates two held subplots and annotations (lines 18-42), then loads and overlays snapshots 0200, 0300, and 0400 on the same axes (lines 44-73).

equations.ref: Grid A coordinate vector derived only from snapshot 0100
Grid B coordinate vector derived only from snapshot 0100
Grid B coordinates translated before plotting

unresolved: Cross-snapshot range defect: x1 and x2 are computed once from the lengths of snapshot 0100 on lines 14-15, but z1 and z2 are replaced by snapshots 0200/0300/0400 on lines 45-46, 56-57, and 66-67 without recomputing coordinates. Any later snapshot length change causes plot dimension errors or assigns coordinates from the wrong grid extent.
Portability defect: both input directories are hard-coded absolute paths under one user's home directory on lines 2-3, with no existence or load-error checks.

The Grid B data origin is shifted to 2004 on line 17 while the annotated nesting boundary is drawn at x=2000 on lines 26 and 38; the four-unit gap may represent grid staggering, but no comment states the intended interface convention.
The annotations label the four suffixes as t=100s through t=400s on lines 39-42, but the code does not read time metadata or establish that file suffixes are seconds.

The code assumes each loaded eta file is a vector compatible with length-based row coordinate construction; matrix-shaped files can make plot orientation/length semantics differ, and no shape validation is performed.
